confirmed.title: JS normalizers lack the 'unrecognized payload' guard -> empty ok:true extractions
confirmed.description: rca_core/extractor.py flags `truncated_or_unrecognized_payload` when the parsed dict has none of the documented root keys (sections/species_ranges/biozones/other_fossils/confidence) and no _array_root, and extract_range_chart flips that to ok=False, error_key='err.parse' (extractor.py:867-879). None of the four JS normalizers (rcaNormalizeResult, rcaNormalizeColumnarResult, rcaNormalizeAbundanceResult, rcaNormalizePhylogeneticTreeResult) performs this check. Concrete failure: in direct/browser mode the model returns valid-but-off-schema JSON - e.g. a refusal `{"message":"Sorry, I cannot read the text in this image clearly enough."}` or a truncated response whose only balanced fragments are inner row objects (safeJsonLoads Level-4 rescues e.g. `{"species":"Orbicularia striata",...}` with no payload keys). Verified in Node: rcaNormalizeResult on both inputs returns all-empty tables, and extractRangeChart returns them as ok:true. For the refusal case there is NO alert at all (truncated=false, no partialFailures): the researcher sees a successful extraction with zero taxa and can export it, while backend mode would have shown err.parse. For the truncated case only the err.truncated warning shows, but state.result is still set to the empty/partial rescue and rendered/exportable.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Mirror extractor.py:629-634 + 867-879: in each JS normalizer detect a non-empty parsed dict with no recognized root keys (and no _array_root) and either return a marker that extractRangeChart converts to `{ok:false, errorKey:'err.parse', warning:'rescued inner object: unusable'}`, or refuse the empty rescue when truncated=true.
confirmed.scientific_impact: Direct-mode runs can present an empty or rescued-fragment extraction as a successful complete result; a researcher could log 'no taxa' or export an empty CSV for a chart that actually contains data.
confirmed.verdict_reasoning: Verified end-to-end in Node with a mocked fetch: a refusal payload {"message":"Sorry, I cannot read the text..."} passes safeJsonLoads (Level-3 strict parse), rcaNormalizeResult builds all-empty tables (message survives only in _extras, which app.js never inspects), and extractRangeChart returns {ok:true, errorKey:undefined}. Python parity confirmed: normalize_result adds 'truncated_or_unrecognized_payload' (rca_core/extractor.py:629-634) and extract_range_chart flips it to ok=False err.parse (extractor.py:871-879) — verified by running normalize_result on the same payload. app.js (lines 680-702) shows alerts only for chimera_warnings / partialFailures / truncated; for the refusal case none of those are set, so the researcher sees a successful extraction with zero taxa, and it is stored in state.result (app.js:658) and exportable. In the truncated-rescue variant (truncated=true) only the err.truncated warning fires while state.result is still set to the empty rescue. None of the four JS normalizers contains a root-key sanity check. Severity HIGH (not CRITICAL): the emptiness is visible in the rendered tables, but the success status and exportability diverge from backend mode under realistic VLM-refusal/truncation conditions.

confirmed.title: Direct-path phylo normalizer drops metadata.taxon_group/root_name/total_nodes that Python preserves
confirmed.description: The phylogenetic prompt instructs the model to emit metadata.taxon_group, metadata.root_name, metadata.total_nodes (and a root-level "version": "1"). Python's normalizer preserves everything outside the six new keys: 'for k, v in metadata_raw.items(): if k not in NEW_META_KEYS: metadata[k] = v' (rca_core/extractor.py:1620-1622) and keeps root extras as _extras (extractor.py:1633-1644). The JS normalizer rebuilds metadata with ONLY title/extraction_timestamp/tree_type/scale/rooted/source (js/minimax.js:727-735) and drops the root extras entirely - taxon_group, root_name, total_nodes and version are silently lost in the pure-browser path. Concrete failure: a researcher extracts a tree in direct mode and exports JSON for a paper/data deposit - the root taxon name and clade are missing, while the identical extraction via the backend contains them; auditors comparing records see endpoint-dependent fields.
confirmed.evidence: js/minimax.js:728-735 'metadata: { title: ..., extraction_timestamp: ..., tree_type: ..., scale: ..., rooted: ..., source: ... }' (no carry-over) vs rca_core/extractor.py:1620-1622 'for k, v in metadata_raw.items(): if k not in NEW_META_KEYS: metadata[k] = v'
confirmed.suggested_fix: After building the six canonical metadata keys in rcaNormalizePhylogeneticTreeResult, copy any remaining metadata_raw keys into metadata (and carry unknown root keys into _extras), mirroring extractor.py.
confirmed.scientific_impact: Loss of tree provenance metadata (root taxon, taxon group, node count) in browser-side extractions - endpoint-dependent data loss in research-grade outputs.
confirmed.verdict_reasoning: The shared prompt explicitly instructs the model to emit metadata.taxon_group, metadata.total_nodes, metadata.root_name and a root-level "version":"1" (js/prompt.js:248-255, rca_core/prompt.py:219-223). Python preserves them: extractor.py:1620-1622 copies every metadata key outside NEW_META_KEYS, and extractor.py:1633-1644 carries unknown root keys (e.g. version) into _extras; project tests assert this contract (tests/test_phylogenetic_tree.py:132-133). rcaNormalizePhylogeneticTreeResult (js/minimax.js:727-740) rebuilds metadata with only title/extraction_timestamp/tree_type/scale/rooted/source and returns no _extras. Verified in Node: input with metadata {taxon_group:'Radiolaria', total_nodes:3, root_name:'Spasmaria', image_source:'fig3.png'} and root version:'1' normalizes to metadata {title:'', extraction_timestamp, tree_type:'', scale:'', rooted:true, source:'fig3.png'} — taxon_group, root_name, total_nodes and version are all absent from the output. (image_source survives only via the source fallback mapping.) Failure scenario: researcher runs phylogenetic extraction in direct/browser mode and exports the JSON for a paper deposit — root taxon name, clade and node count are silently missing, while the identical extraction via the backend contains them. Endpoint-dependent loss of schema-documented provenance fields in realistic use: HIGH upheld.

confirmed.title: ICS 2024 table has stale/wrong stage boundaries (Emsian, Famennian, Rhaetian, ...)
confirmed.description: The file header claims 'Bundled ICS 2024 subset' but many Paleozoic/early-Mesozoic boundaries match pre-2018 charts, not ICS v2024/12. Confirmed wrong values (table -> ICS 2024/12): Emsian base 401.8 -> 410.62 (line 39); Famennian base 367.1 -> 372.15 (line 40); Rhaetian base 208.5 -> 205.7, new GSSP ratified 2024 (line 75); Olenekian base 249.7 -> 251.2 (line 67); Kungurian base 279.5 -> 283.3 (line 56); Pragian base 410.8 -> 413.02 (line 72); Wordian base 268.8 -> 266.9 (line 99); Capitanian base 265.1 -> 264.28 (line 27); 'Stage 5'/Wuliuan base 509.0 -> 506.5 (line 87); Sakmarian base 295.5 -> 295.0 (line 78); Anisian base 245.9 -> 246.7 (line 12); Lochkovian base 419.2 -> 419.62 (line 60); Drumian base 504.2 -> 504.5 (line 37). Consumer impact (js/quality.js _resolveAgeBound, lines 149-225): stage-name bounds resolve to (top_ma+base_ma)/2 midpoints used by the FAD<LAD check in scoreAccuracy. DEMONSTRATED: a scientifically valid range (FAD 'Emsian', LAD '400 Ma'; Emsian spans 410.62-393.47 so 400 Ma is a valid LAD) is flagged quality.fad_lt_lad and the accuracy score drops 1.0 -> 0.5 because the wrong Emsian midpoint (397.55 vs correct ~402.0) falls below 400. Conversely, real inversions spanning the shifted midpoints can pass unflagged. Explicit Ma values between 401.8-410.62 also map to the wrong stage (e.g. 405 Ma -> Pragian instead of Emsian). rca_core/resources/ics_2024.json holds identical wrong values (verified byte-equal via diff), so both ends must be corrected. Key boundaries verified correct: K/Pg 66.0, T/J 201.4, J/K 145.0, P/T 251.9, Calabrian 0.774/1.8, Gelasian 1.8/2.588, Holocene 0.0117, Cambrian base 538.8.
confirmed.evidence: "Emsian": {top_ma: 393.3, base_ma: 401.8, era: "Paleozoic"}, ... "Famennian": {top_ma: 358.9, base_ma: 367.1, ...}, ... "Rhaetian": {top_ma: 201.4, base_ma: 208.5, ...}
confirmed.suggested_fix: Sync rca_core/resources/ics_2024.json and js/ics_table.js to ICS v2024/12 values (Emsian base 410.62, Famennian base 372.15, Rhaetian base 205.7, Olenekian 251.2, Kungurian 283.3, Pragian 413.02, Wordian 266.9, Capitanian 264.28, Wuliuan 506.5, Sakmarian 295.0, Anisian 246.7, Lochkovian 419.62, Drumian 504.5) and re-run the chain check; add a test asserting a valid 'Emsian'->'400 Ma' range is not flagged.
confirmed.scientific_impact: Quality grading of real research extractions is computed against an incorrect timescale: valid species ranges are flagged as FAD<LAD violations and accuracy scores halved (demonstrated), while Ma-to-stage resolution is off by up to ~9 Myr in the Devonian. Downstream researchers relying on the quality badge to accept/reject extractions get systematically wrong triage for Devonian/Permian/Triassic material.
confirmed.verdict_reasoning: Verified against external ICS v2024/12 sources (PBDB timescale citing ICS v2024/12, Wikipedia Early Devonian/Wuliuan/Drumian, Episodes 2025 chart-review paper): v2024/12 gives Lochkovian base 419.62, Pragian 413.02, Emsian 410.62, Famennian 372.15 (Frasnian 382.31), Wuliuan 506.5, Drumian 504.5, Rhaetian 205.7 (GSSP ratified 2024), and GTS2020-based Permian/Triassic values (Kungurian 283.3, Sakmarian 295.0, Wordian 266.9, Capitanian 264.28, Anisian 246.7, Olenekian 251.2). js/ics_table.js instead holds 419.2/410.8/401.8/367.1/382.7/509.0/504.2/208.5 and 279.5/295.5/268.8/265.1/245.9/249.7 — pre-GTS2020 values, despite the 'Bundled ICS 2024 subset' header. rca_core/resources/ics_2024.json was spot-checked and carries the identical stale values (Emsian 393.3-401.8, Famennian 358.9-367.1, Rhaetian 201.4-208.5, Olenekian 245.9-249.7, Kungurian 273.0-279.5, Wordian 265.1-268.8, Capitanian 259.51-265.1, Sakmarian 290.0-295.5, Anisian 241.5-245.9, Lochkovian 410.8-419.2, Pragian 401.8-410.8, Drumian 500.5-504.2), so both ends are wrong in parity. Concrete failure traced in js/quality.js: _resolveAgeBound (lines 204-208) maps a bare stage name to the midpoint (top_ma+base_ma)/2, giving Emsian 397.55. A valid extraction row {range_base:'Emsian', range_top:'400 Ma'} enters the age branch of scoreAccuracy (lines 378-388) because _looksLikeAge('400 Ma') is true; baseR.ma=397.55 < topR.ma=400 fires quality.fad_lt_lad and the FAD/LAD check scores 0 (accuracy 1.0 -> 0.5 with two checks), whereas with correct v2024/12 values (Emsian 410.62-393.47, midpoint ~402.05 > 400) it passes unflagged. The reverse error also holds where bases shifted younger: Rhaetian old midpoint 204.95 vs correct 203.55 lets a real inversion (FAD Rhaetian, LAD '204 Ma') pass unflagged. Explicit-Ma stage naming is also wrong: loop at lines 159-161 maps 405 Ma to Pragian (401.8-410.8 contains it) instead of Emsian (note: only the returned name, since scoring compares .ma — a minor overstatement in the finding). Python parity confirmed: rca_core/standards/ics.py computes the same midpoint ((base+top)/2, lines 364 and 399) from the same stale JSON, so server-side scoring errs identically; js/app.js:671 calls scoreRangeChart for the live UI quality badge. HIGH, not CRITICAL, because the extracted scientific data itself is not corrupted — the defect is systematic wrong quality triage (false flags / missed inversions / halved accuracy) for Devonian/Permian/Triassic material, which is realistic core use of this paleontology tool.

confirmed.title: Columnar-section render/CSV drops all bed-level data (lithology_blocks/age_units/samples)
confirmed.description: In columnar_section mode the sections row extractor emits only id/group/thickness_m/coordinates_text. The per-section nested arrays lithology_blocks (bed-by-bed lithology with range_base_idx/range_top_idx), age_units (age labels with bounds) and samples (bed_idx + fossil_marker + citation) — the primary scientific content of a columnar section per the extraction schema (js/prompt.js:148-166) — are rendered in no table and exported in no CSV/TSV. Verified empirically: rcaRenderResults on a columnar payload containing samples:[{bed_idx:5,fossil_marker:'J',ref:'Kamata1996'}], age_units:[{label:'JurassicUnit',...}], lithology_blocks:[{pattern:'chert',range_top_idx:8,range_base_idx:1}] renders none of those strings (HTML probes returned false for all), and rcaBuildTableExport(data,'sections').rows = [["1","Ki-1","Kurohone","500 m","nv"]]. A researcher downloading the sections CSV gets an empty shell of the figure; the data survives only in the full-JSON export. rca_core/exporter.py has the same gap, so this is an unflagged lossy export on both ends.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add flattened tables (or repeated rows) for lithology_blocks/age_units/samples keyed by section id, mirroring the schema fields, so the CSV/TSV copy-download paths include the bed-level data; at minimum surface them in the UI.
confirmed.scientific_impact: CSV/TSV exports of columnar sections silently omit every lithologic unit, age unit and fossil-sample horizon — the core stratigraphic observations of the figure — risking analysis based on a drastically incomplete dataset.
confirmed.verdict_reasoning: Verified in code, could not refute. table.js columnar branch (lines 69-121) defines only 4 tables; the sections row extractor `cols4` (lines 77-82) emits exactly [sec.id, sec.group, sec.thickness_m, sec.coordinates_text]. The columnar normalizer (minimax.js:513-529) preserves lithology_blocks/age_units/samples as first-class per-section arrays (normBlocks/normUnits/normSamples at lines 460-489), and prompt.js:147-160 defines them as the primary per-section scientific content (bed-by-bed lithology ranges, age-unit bounds, fossil sample horizons with bed_idx/fossil_marker/ref). A repo-wide grep shows those keys appear in js/ only in minimax.js (normalization) and quality.js (scoring) — rcaRenderResults (table.js:273 loop) and rcaBuildTableExport (table.js:373, used by the Copy-TSV and Download-CSV handlers in app.js:819-834) are the only table render/export paths and neither touches them; rcaRenderViz is a documented no-op. Python parity gap confirmed: rca_core/exporter.py:_columnar_section_tables (lines 271-280) exports the same 4 columns only. Failure scenario: extract a columnar figure producing sections:[{id:'Ki-1', group:'Kurohone', thickness_m:'500 m', coordinates_text:'nv', lithology_blocks:[{pattern:'chert',range_top_idx:8,range_base_idx:1}], age_units:[{label:'JurassicUnit',...}], samples:[{bed_idx:5,fossil_marker:'J',ref:'Kamata1996'}]}] → the UI renders one 4-cell row and the downloaded sections.csv contains only index/id/group/thickness/coordinates; every lithologic unit, age unit and fossil-sample horizon is absent from all tables and CSVs, surviving only in Export-all JSON. HIGH (not CRITICAL): the data is not corrupted and remains reachable via the full-JSON export, but the core stratigraphic observations of a columnar extraction are silently omitted from every table/CSV path in realistic research use.

The prompt explicitly instructs the model to put uncertainty remarks in `note` and taphonomic classification in endpoint_kind/occurrence_mode ('UNCERTAINTY IS DATA'), yet the rendered table, Copy-TSV and Download-CSV all silently drop them — a researcher exporting to CSV loses the uncertainty/taphonomy annotations with no indication. const speciesRow = (r) => [r.species, r.section, r.range_base, r.range_top, r.biozone];

confirmed.verdict_reasoning: Verified in code, could not refute. table.js:158-159 renders/exports exactly 5 cells per species row: speciesCols=['col.species','col.section','col.rangeBase','col.rangeTop','col.biozone'], speciesRow=(r)=>[r.species,r.section,r.range_base,r.range_top,r.biozone]. The normalizer promotes 13+ fields to first-class row keys (minimax.js SP_KNOWN lines 261-267; row construction lines 329-350: author/year/author_year, range_top_bed/range_base_bed, range_top_idx/range_base_idx, endpoint_kind, occurrence_mode, confidence, note), and the prompt explicitly mandates them: prompt.js:69-70 (endpoint_kind/occurrence_mode enums), :73 (note), :103 (author_year), :106 'UNCERTAINTY IS DATA... NEVER default an unreadable classification to observed or in_situ', plus the degradation clause (prompt.js:36) routing ambiguity into note/confidence. The same 5-column config drives the rendered table, Copy-TSV and Download-CSV (rcaBuildTableExport, app.js:819-834), so all three silently drop the 8 annotation fields. The biozone claim also checks: table.js:197 row=[b.name,b.section,b.age,b.thickness_m] drops zone_type, which the normalizer enforces/infers (minimax.js:311 BZ_KNOWN, line 392). confirmed.title: Phylo multi-run merge: is_leaf becomes string "true" in JS, stays bool in Python
confirmed.description: In the phylogenetic_tree multi-run merge, node fields outside strModeFields go through the scalar merge. JS mergeScalarField stringifies booleans ('if (typeof v === "string" || typeof v === "number" || typeof v === "boolean") { const s = String(v).trim(); ... }', js/aggregate.js:119-121), so rcaAggMode returns the string 'true'/'false'. Python _merge_scalar_field keeps bools in a separate list and 'return[s] the bool directly' (rca_core/aggregate.py:146-166). Verified by running both mergers on identical 2-run phylo inputs: JS emitted is_leaf:"true" (string), Python emitted is_leaf:True (bool). Concrete failure: a researcher runs a phylogenetic tree with runs>1 in direct mode; the merged nodes[] and any JSON/Newick export carry is_leaf as a JSON string, while the same extraction via the backend carries a real boolean - downstream consumers checking === true (or strict schemas) silently see every leaf as not-a-leaf in the browser path only.
confirmed.evidence: js/aggregate.js:119 'if (typeof v === "string" || typeof v === "number" || typeof v === "boolean") { const s = String(v).trim();' vs rca_core/aggregate.py:159-166 'if bools: ... mode_bool = Counter(bools).most_common(1)[0][0]; return mode_bool'. Empirical: JS is_leaf: "true" string | PY is_leaf: True bool
confirmed.suggested_fix: Mirror Python: in mergeScalarField/mergeFieldAcrossRuns keep an all-boolean fast path that returns the boolean mode (true/false) instead of String(v), matching _merge_scalar_field.
confirmed.scientific_impact: Phylogenetic tree leaf/internal classification is corrupted to strings in browser-side multi-run merges, changing exported tree topology metadata depending on which endpoint produced the merge.
confirmed.verdict_reasoning: Verified in code and empirically. Phylo keymap strModeFields is ['name'] only (js/aggregate.js:259), so is_leaf enters the generic per-field merge (aggregate.js:455-468) → mergeFieldAcrossRuns → all-primitive branch (aggregate.js:206) → mergeScalarField, which stringifies booleans: 'if (typeof v === "string" || typeof v === "number" || typeof v === "boolean") { const s = String(v).trim(); ...' (aggregate.js:119-121). Python _merge_scalar_field (rca_core/aggregate.py:146-166) keeps bools in a separate list and returns the real bool. Reachable in the actual app: both normalizers emit genuine booleans (js/minimax.js:691-705; rca_core/extractor.py:1574-1592) and direct/proxy multi-run merge at js/app.js:583 applies no re-normalization. Empirical run of both mergers on identical 2-run phylo input: JS emitted is_leaf "false"/"true" (typeof string), Python emitted False/True (bool). Concrete failure sequence: researcher selects phylogenetic-tree mode, runs ≥2 in direct mode; merged nodes carry is_leaf strings; js/table.js:148 renders the leaf column via truthiness (n.is_leaf ? 'Y' : 'N'), and the string "false" is truthy, so EVERY internal node is silently shown (and exported to CSV/TSV through the same row builder, app.js:822-833) as a leaf 'Y', while the backend path correctly shows 'N' — endpoint-dependent, silently wrong leaf/internal classification. (Note: the in-app visible direction is the opposite of the finding's '=== true sees every leaf as not-a-leaf' — truthiness consumers see every INTERNAL node as a leaf — but the data is corrupted either way, and strict ===true consumers of the JSON export do see zero leaves.) Kept at HIGH rather than CRITICAL: real wrong results under realistic research use, but confined to phylo mode + runs>1 + browser transport, one field, with the semantic value recoverable.

confirmed.title: Abundance sum-to-100 penalty never applied in JS accuracy score
confirmed.description: Python computes accuracy = passed/checks first, then subtracts the sum-to-100 deduction from the final score ('score = max(0.0, score - deduction)', rca_core/quality.py:536-539; checks==0 -> score=1.0 at lines 529-532). JS applies the deduction to 'passed' BEFORE division ('passed = Math.max(0.0, passed - deduction)', js/quality.js:580) and then returns 1.0 unconditionally when checks===0 (js/quality.js:595). A typical abundance result has zero other accuracy checks, so JS accuracy stays 1.0 while Python drops to 0.95-0.70. Verified on an identical abundance payload with a 60% level sum: JS composite 0.975/A vs Python 0.955/A; with a slightly lower base score the 0.4-weighted delta (up to 0.12) flips grades (e.g. 0.88 B vs 1.00 A). Concrete failure: a pollen diagram where the extracted taxa sum to <95% per level (the norm when only readable columns are extracted) gets a clean quality badge in the browser but a penalized one from the server/history record.
confirmed.evidence: js/quality.js:580 'passed = Math.max(0.0, passed - deduction);' + :595 'if (checks === 0) return [1.0, issues];' vs rca_core/quality.py:538-539 'deduction = min(0.3, 0.05 * len(sum_violations)); score = max(0.0, score - deduction)'. Empirical: JS 0.975 vs PY 0.955 on same input
confirmed.suggested_fix: Compute the accuracy ratio first, then subtract the deduction from the ratio (as Python does), instead of subtracting from 'passed' before division.
confirmed.scientific_impact: Quality grades for abundance diagrams are systematically inflated in the pure-browser path, hiding percentage-sum inconsistencies that flag unreliable extractions.
confirmed.verdict_reasoning: Verified in code. Python (_score_accuracy, rca_core/quality.py:529-539) first computes score = passed/checks (or 1.0 when checks==0), THEN applies 'deduction = min(0.3, 0.05 * len(sum_violations)); score = max(0.0, score - deduction)'. JS (js/quality.js:577-596) subtracts the deduction from 'passed' BEFORE division ('passed = Math.max(0.0, passed - deduction)') and then returns '[1.0, issues]' when checks===0 (line 595). Concrete failure: a pure abundance result (no species_ranges, no section blocks with idx fields, no era/stage text) has checks===0 in scoreAccuracy; with a level whose '%' abundances sum to e.g. 60 (outside 95-105), JS returns accuracy 1.0 while Python returns 1.0-0.05=0.95. Even when checks>0 the math diverges: (passed-d)/checks != passed/checks - d for checks>=2 (e.g. checks=2, passed=2, d=0.05: JS 0.975 vs PY 0.95). With accuracy weight 0.40 the composite delta is up to 0.12, enough to flip A/B grades. The reviewer's empirical 0.975/0.955 composites are consistent with structure=0.75 + accuracy divergence. The file header explicitly promises byte-for-byte parity, so this is a genuine parity defect, not a design choice. HIGH (not CRITICAL): the wrong number is a quality badge/meta-assessment, not the extracted scientific data itself, but it occurs under realistic abundance-mode use.

confirmed.title: Dict-shaped other_fossils items become literal "[object Object]" taxa in tables/exports
confirmed.description: rcaNormalizeResult stringifies every other_fossils element via asStr = (v)=>String(v). When the model emits dict entries in other_fossils (a normal path) or a top-level array whose items classify as other_fossils (rcaUnwrapArrayRoot pushes the raw objects into dist.other_fossils at lines 185-189), String(dict) yields the literal '[object Object]'. Verified in Node: input `{"other_fossils":["Ammonites sp.",{"taxon":"trace fossils"}]}` normalizes to `["Ammonites sp.","[object Object]"]`, and `[{"label":"Spiriferina rostrata"},{"label":"Productus cf. semireticulatus"}]` becomes `["[object Object]","[object Object]"]`. Python parity (extractor.py:731-734) keeps only `isinstance(x, str)` items, i.e. drops dicts instead of fabricating names. These strings render in the taxa table and are exported to CSV/JSON for research use.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Filter to string items like Python (`typeof x === 'string'`), or serialize dict items to a meaningful label (e.g. x.taxon/x.label/x.name) before stringifying.
confirmed.scientific_impact: Fabricated taxon names ('[object Object]') can enter exported datasets and downstream analyses; JS output diverges from the Python export for the same model response.
confirmed.verdict_reasoning: Verified both sides empirically. JS: rcaNormalizeResult maps every other_fossils element through asStr=String(v) (js/minimax.js:398-400); Node test on {"other_fossils":["Ammonites sp.",{"taxon":"trace fossils"}]} yields ["Ammonites sp.","[object Object]"], and a top-level array of {label:...} dicts (rcaUnwrapArrayRoot pushes them into dist.other_fossils via rcaClassifyArrayItem's label/taxon fallback, minimax.js:235-237) yields ["[object Object]","[object Object]"]. Python: normalize_result keeps only string items for a named other_fossils array ([s(x) for x in of if isinstance(x, str)], extractor.py:731-738) — verified: the dict entry is dropped, output ['Ammonites sp.']. confirmed.title: Direct mode follows redirects: x-api-key forwarded to arbitrary redirect targets (no scheme/host pinning)
confirmed.description: The direct-mode fetch uses the default redirect:'follow' and sends the API key as a custom header. The F-8/SSRF guards (lines 1020-1046) validate only the user-typed URL: they cannot see the redirect destination, so an entered https endpoint may redirect to plaintext http:// (key transmitted in cleartext, defeating the stated 'Enforce HTTPS' protection) or to an internal/metadata host (169.254.169.254 etc.) that the same code claims to block. The backend path defends against exactly this via rca_core.ssrf.validate_endpoint + pinned_endpoint_ip (server.py:411-435); the browser path has no equivalent. Scenario: a researcher configures a third-party relay/proxy (the proxyUrl field exists precisely for this); a compromised or open-redirecting relay 302s the POST and captures the LLM API key.

confirmed.scientific_impact: none

Mechanism confirmed against the WHATWG Fetch spec and implementations: on cross-origin redirects browsers strip only the Authorization header (whatwg/fetch#944, PR #1544, shipped in Chrome 119); custom headers such as x-api-key are re-sent to the redirect target (the same leak class tracked in axios#10711 and Chromium issue 492178064). So an https endpoint the researcher configures (proxyUrl exists precisely for third-party relays) can 302 the POST and the key is delivered to the redirect target; a malicious relay can answer the CORS preflight and capture the key, and an https→http downgrade transmits it in cleartext where the page context permits. MEDIUM upheld: genuine security gap that defeats the file's own F-8/SSRF protections, but exploitation requires a user-configured endpoint that redirects maliciously, and the key is already entrusted to that endpoint by configuration.

Failure scenario: browser-only user (file:// or proxy → direct transport) runs a multi-run extraction (up to 5 concurrent requests); provider returns transient 429/502/503 or a network blip; the whole extraction fails instantly with err.429/err.network where the backend path would have retried and succeeded. Severity stays MEDIUM: the failure is loud, user-recoverable, and produces no wrong scientific data (fail-fast, not fail-wrong), but it is a real robustness/parity gap under realistic direct-mode use; the predicate defect itself is latent (module is dead code today) but would silently break any future predicate-driven retry wiring.

confirmed.title: English quality.range_top_lt_base message is semantically inverted
confirmed.description: The check fires when the range top is OLDER than the base: quality.py bed branch triggers on top < base with beds 1-indexed from bottom (younger = larger index), and the Ma branch triggers on base_ma < top_ma (rca_core/quality.py:358-384). zh ('部分物种的 LAD（末现）早于 FAD（首现）') and ja ('LAD（最終出現）が FAD（最初出現）より早い') correctly describe the violation (last appearance before first appearance). The English string instead says 'range top younger than their range base' — which is the NORMAL, expected ordering. An English-UI researcher hovering the quality badge reads a harmless statement for a real FAD/LAD inversion warning.
confirmed.evidence: 'quality.range_top_lt_base': 'Some species have range top younger than their range base',
confirmed.suggested_fix: Change to e.g. 'Some species have range top OLDER than their range base (LAD earlier than FAD)' to match zh/ja and the actual check.
confirmed.scientific_impact: English users are told a biostratigraphic inconsistency warning describes a normal condition, so genuine FAD/LAD inversions in the extracted ranges may be ignored.
confirmed.verdict_reasoning: The check fires when the range TOP is OLDER than the base, and the en string describes the opposite (normal) ordering. rca_core/quality.py:358-366: bed branch fires the warning when `top < base`, with beds 1-indexed from the bottom and younger = LARGER index (comment at quality.py:339-342 and prompt.js:175 'Bed/horizon indices are 1-indexed from BOTTOM (oldest = 1)'), so a smaller top index means the top bed is OLDER. The Ma branch (quality.py:377-384) fires on `base_ma < top_ma`, i.e. FAD younger than LAD — again top older than base. zh ('部分物种的 LAD（末现）早于 FAD（首现）', js/i18n.js:234) and ja ('一部の種で LAD（最終出現）が FAD（最初出現）より早い', js/i18n.js:702) correctly describe LAD earlier than FAD. The en string at js/i18n.js:469 says 'Some species have range top younger than their range base' — 'top younger than base' is the expected, valid ordering, so the English tooltip states a harmless condition for a real violation. Concrete failure sequence: (1) researcher uses the English UI with the same-origin backend; (2) the LLM extracts a species with range_top='Bed 3', range_base='Bed 7' (or inverted ages); (3) server.py:_safe_score_range_chart → rca_core.quality.score_range_chart appends {severity:'warning', msg_key:'quality.range_top_lt_base'} (quality.py:363-366); (4) js/table.js:247-262 builds the quality-badge tooltip via t(msg_key), rendering the inverted English sentence. The researcher sees a warning badge whose explanation text describes normal stratigraphy, so a genuine FAD/LAD inversion may be dismissed. (The pure-browser scorer path uses the correctly-worded quality.fad_lt_lad key, so only server-scored results expose this.) Impact is a misleading warning description, not wrong data or a wrong score — MEDIUM stands.

confirmed.title: Cross-era check regex omits 'paleocene', missing K/Pg-style era mixes
confirmed.description: The Cenozoic era regex lists paleogene|neogene|quaternary|pleistocene|holocene|eocene|oligocene|miocene|pliocene but not 'paleocene' (all other Cenozoic epochs are present). A section whose age blocks mix Mesozoic and Paleocene labels (e.g. 'Upper Cretaceous' + 'Paleocene' across the K/Pg boundary) registers only {Mesozoic}, so the cross-era consistency warning (quality.ages_inconsistent) is silently skipped. rca_core/quality.py _CENOZOIC_RE (lines 445-447) has the identical omission, so both paths misbehave. Concrete failure: a columnar section with age_units ['Upper Cretaceous', 'Paleocene', 'Eocene'] should flag era-mixing scrutiny; instead only the Eocene block contributes 'Cenozoic' and the Cretaceous/Paleocene mix passes - and if 'Eocene' is absent, no warning fires at all.
confirmed.evidence: const cenozoicRe2 = /\b(paleogene|neogene|quaternary|pleistocene|holocene|eocene|oligocene|miocene|pliocene)\b/i;
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add 'paleocene' to the Cenozoic regex in both js/quality.js and rca_core/quality.py (parity requirement).
confirmed.scientific_impact: Sections spanning the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary expressed with epoch names escape the era-consistency sanity check, so an obvious stratigraphic inconsistency (or a genuinely boundary-crossing section that deserves review) is neither flagged nor reviewed.
confirmed.verdict_reasoning: Factual omission verified: js/quality.js:467 cenozoicRe2 lists paleogene|neogene|quaternary|pleistocene|holocene|eocene|oligocene|miocene|pliocene but not 'paleocene'; grep -i 'paleocene' over both js/quality.js and rca_core/quality.py returns nothing (rca_core/quality.py:445-447 _CENOZOIC_RE has the identical list). 'Paleocene' matches no alternative ('paleogene' differs at the 6th char and \b blocks substring matches) and matches none of the Paleozoic/Mesozoic regexes, so a section with age blocks ['Upper Cretaceous','Paleocene'] yields eras={Mesozoic} only and quality.ages_inconsistent never fires. However, downgraded to LOW: (1) both paths share the omission, so there is NO endpoint/parity divergence — the stated audit category concern (parity) does not apply; (2) the reviewer's three-label example (Cretaceous+Paleocene+Eocene) actually DOES fire the warning via Eocene, so the miss only occurs when 'Paleocene' is the sole Cenozoic term; (3) the check is advisory and when it fires it also deducts 0.5*count from the accuracy check (js/quality.js:500 / py:480), so missing it for legitimate K/Pg boundary sections avoids an unjustified penalty as often as it hides a problem. Minor edge-case impact.

plausible.title: Structured-field dedup signature: JS keeps numeric vs string duplicates Python merges
plausible.description: mergeStructuredField dedups list-of-dicts items (columnar lithology_blocks/age_units/samples, etc.) by rcaStructDedupKey, which serializes numbers as 'k:8' and strings as 'k:"8"' (js/aggregate.js:54-64). Python's _merge_structured_field coerces ALL values to str first - 'P1-11 fix: coerce all values to str before repr so that {"a": 8} and {"a": "8"} produce the same signature and merge' (rca_core/aggregate.py:227-233). Verified: merging two columnar runs where one emits lithology_blocks[0].range_top_idx=8 and the other "8" yields 2 blocks in JS and 1 block in Python. Concrete failure: the VLM flips a bed index between int and string across runs (common LLM instability); the browser merge emits a duplicated lithology block (double-counted stratigraphic interval in exported columns) while the backend merge collapses it - endpoint-dependent aggregated science.
plausible.evidence: js/aggregate.js:60 'if (typeof v === 'number') return k + ':' + String(v);' (strings use JSON.stringify -> quoted) vs rca_core/aggregate.py:230 'sig = repr(sorted(((k, str(val)) for k, val in item.items())))'. Empirical: JS lithology_blocks count: 2, PY lithology_blocks count: 1
plausible.suggested_fix: Make rcaStructDedupKey coerce every scalar with String(v) only (no JSON.stringify quoting for strings), matching Python's str(val) coercion.
plausible.scientific_impact: Duplicated vs collapsed stratigraphic blocks/intervals in merged columnar sections depending on endpoint - direct data-shape corruption of the merged scientific record.
plausible.verdict_reasoning: The code-level divergence is real but the stated failure scenario is blocked by the app's normalization layer, and the reachable residual manifests in the opposite direction. Code: rcaStructDedupKey serializes numbers as k:8 and strings as k:"8" (js/aggregate.js:59-60), while Python coerces every value with str() before the signature (rca_core/aggregate.py:227-233), so {"a":8} and {"a":"8"} merge in Python. However, in the real pipeline every run is normalized before merging on BOTH endpoints: the browser path always runs rcaNormalizeColumnarResult (js/minimax.js:1201-1208), whose asInt coerces range_top_idx/range_base_idx/bed_idx to int or null (minimax.js:446-450, 460-489); the backend runs normalize_columnar_result with the equivalent fi() coercion (rca_core/extractor.py:975-1000). All three merge call sites (js/app.js:583 direct mode, server.py:1183, gui.py:1730/gui_fluent.py:300) consume normalized data only. Empirical check: with normalized inputs (8 vs 8) BOTH mergers return 1 lithology block; the reviewer's 2-vs-1 reproduction requires feeding raw un-normalized dicts straight to the mergers, which the app never does — a VLM int/string flip on a bed index is coerced to the same int before the merger ever sees it, so no duplicated stratigraphic block occurs in the browser. Residual legitimate parity gap (why not FALSE_POSITIVE): the only un-coerced channel is the carried _extras dict; rcaStructDedupKey stringifies any dict value to '[object Object]' (aggregate.js:61), ignoring extras content, while Python's str(dict) distinguishes them — empirical: identical blocks whose _extras holds 5 vs "5" collapse to 1 block in JS but stay 2 in Python. That is the opposite direction from the claim and only affects items differing solely in non-schema metadata, hence downgraded to MEDIUM (edge-case parity divergence, endpoint-dependent block counts) rather than HIGH.

plausible.title: SUM-TO-100 check applied unconditionally; false penalties on subset-sum diagrams
plausible.description: scoreAccuracy sums all abundance_unit='%' entries per level and deducts up to 0.3 from accuracy when the sum is outside 95-105. In standard palynological practice percentages are frequently computed on a SUBSET sum (upland pollen sum excluding aquatics/spores, or a diatom sum with exotic pollen plotted alongside), so a correctly extracted level can legitimately total far outside 100+/-5. Concrete failure: a pollen diagram with Pinus 45%, Quercus 30%, Poaceae 20% (all on the upland sum, total ~95-100) plus aquatic Nymphaea 25% plotted but excluded from the sum -> extracted sum 120 -> quality.abundance_sum_violation warning + 0.05-0.3 accuracy deduction for a scientifically correct extraction. The prompt (js/prompt.js:235) at least tells the VLM to note discrepancies, but the scorer penalizes regardless, and the same logic exists in rca_core/quality.py (parity), so backend scoring misgrades identically.
plausible.evidence: const s = levelSums[lvl]; if (s < 95 || s > 105) violations.push({sample: levelIds[lvl], sum: s});
plausible.suggested_fix: Soften the check: only penalize when the deviation is large (>15-20) or repeated across most levels, or treat it as info-level unless the prompt-extracted abundance basis indicates a single closed sum; alternatively add an abundance_basis field to the schema and skip the check when taxa are marked excluded-from-sum.
plausible.scientific_impact: Legitimate percentage diagrams (the most common abundance-diagram convention in palynology) are downgraded and flagged as erroneous, biasing researchers against correct extractions of real pollen/diatom data.
plausible.verdict_reasoning: The code behaves exactly as described: js/quality.js:556-592 sums all abundance_unit='%' entries per level and deducts min(0.3, 0.05*violations) whenever a level sum falls outside 95-105, with no opt-out; rca_core/quality.py:_score_abundance_sum (925-962) is identical (parity preserved). The palynological concern is legitimate — percentages computed on a subset sum (upland sum excluding aquatics/spores, diatom sum with exotics plotted) can legitimately total >105, and the extraction prompt ('ONE COLUMN = ONE TAXON... emit one abundances entry for each (taxon, level) intersection') directs the VLM to read ALL columns, so a correct extraction of such a diagram would be penalized. I cannot CONFIRM end-to-end, however: the system's own contract explicitly codifies the rule (js/prompt.js: 'SUM-TO-100. For each level... should equal 100 +/- 5%. If your reading differs significantly, lower the row confidence and note the discrepancy'), so the scorer enforces a stated design contract, and whether real submitted diagrams/VLM outputs actually produce out-of-range sums is data-dependent and unverifiable statically. Note the prompt's escape hatch is also broken (the abundance schema has no per-row confidence or note field — only taxon/site/level/depth/abundance/abundance_unit), which strengthens the concern. Impact is bounded (accuracy deduction capped at 0.3 -> max 0.12 composite, visible warnings showing the computed sum that a specialist can dismiss), so MEDIUM rather than HIGH: a science-validity concern about a heuristic, not silently wrong data.

skipped_unverified.title: Merge schema selection differs: backend uses requested mode, direct path auto-detects shape
skipped_unverified.description: The backend merges with an explicit schema chosen from the REQUESTED mode: 'schema = SCHEMA_BY_MODE.get(mode, RANGE_CHART_SCHEMA); merged = merge_results(ok_datas, total_runs=runs, schema=schema)' (server.py:1182-1183). The direct path ignores the requested mode for merging - app.js:537-538 computes 'km' from RCA_KEYMAP_BY_MODE[chartMode] but never uses it, and app.js:580 merges with 'rcaAutoDetectKeymap(okDatas)' (shape-based). low_severity.title: Direct mode hardcodes the Anthropic wire format and /v1/messages path; backend call omits api_format
low_severity.description: extractRangeChart always builds `target + '/v1/messages'` with x-api-key/anthropic-version headers, regardless of the endpoint actually configured; rca_core supports three wire formats (ANTHROPIC/OPENAI/GEMINI, llm.py:73-75, dispatched in call_llm_api). In backend mode rcaCallBackend's POST body (lines 905-918) never sends `api_format`, and the server falls back to `(req.get('api_format') or 'anthropic')` (server.py:836-840). So a researcher who pastes an OpenAI-compatible (e.g. SiliconFlow `/v1`) or Gemini endpoint gets an opaque failure in both transports (direct mode even hits `.../v1/v1/messages` for endpoints ending in /v1), while the Python GUI supports those providers. Additionally there is no scheme validation: a scheme-less endpoint ('api.example.com/anthropic') fails `new URL()` (hostname ''), skips the SSRF check, and fetch resolves it as a same-origin relative path.

low_severity.title: rcaBuildNewickNode uses the pre-fix escaping that Python explicitly replaced (commas unquoted)
low_severity.description: Python's _build_newick_node was fixed ('Phase M fix', extractor.py:1681-1687) to quote labels via _quote_newick_label because replacing ( ) : with '_' 'loses semantic information', and because labels containing `, ( ) [ ] ; :` must be single-quoted per the Newick spec. The JS mirror still has the old broken behavior: `name.replace(/\(/g,'_').replace(/\)/g,'_').replace(/:/g,'_')` - it mangles names AND leaves commas/semicolons/brackets unescaped, so a taxon name like 'Species A, morphotype B' would split into two Newick subtrees, silently corrupting the tree topology. Currently dead code (no callers in js/ or index.html), so user impact today is zero - but it is exported for future wiring and contradicts the parity contract in its own header comment ('Mirrors Python rca_core.extractor.to_newick()').
low_severity.suggested_fix: Port _quote_newick_label: if the label contains any of `(),[];:` or whitespace, wrap it in single quotes and double embedded single quotes; otherwise emit it unchanged.
low_severity.scientific_impact: If wired into an export path, taxon names with commas/semicolons would produce structurally wrong phylogenetic trees (wrong topology) presented as valid Newick.

low_severity.title: Node support conflates bootstrap % and posterior probability with no type field
low_severity.description: The SUPPORT VALUES rule puts both 'bootstrap %' and 'posterior probability' into the single float `support` with no support_type discriminator: a printed '0.97' (posterior probability) and '97' (bootstrap %) become numerically different but semantically identical entries, while '0.89' vs '89' from two nodes on the same figure cannot be told apart downstream. Consumers comparing or thresholding support values (e.g. 'collapse nodes <70%') will mix scales - a classic error since 0.95 posterior probability is not comparable to 95% bootstrap.
low_severity.evidence: "support": 89 (float, the numeric support value at the node — bootstrap %, posterior probability, or empty when not shown)
low_severity.suggested_fix: Add a support_type field (bootstrap | posterior_probability | other) and instruct the VLM to record which scale is printed (per figure, or per node when mixed).
low_severity.scientific_impact: Node-support statistics can be silently mis-scaled in downstream comparative analyses, misrepresenting clade robustness.

low_severity.title: Holocene subseries stages and Late Pleistocene interval unrepresented
low_severity.description: The 'ICS 2024 subset' contains only 'Holocene' (0-0.0117) and 'Chibanian' (top 0.129), leaving: (1) the official Holocene stages Greenlandian (base 0.0117), Northgrippian (0.0082) and Meghalayan (0.0042) - ratified ICS stages since 2018 - absent, and (2) an internal chain gap 0.0117-0.129 Ma (the informal Upper Pleistocene) between Holocene.base_ma=0.0117 and Chibanian.top_ma=0.129. In js/quality.js _resolveAgeBound, labels like 'Meghalayan', 'Greenlandian' or 'Late Pleistocene' resolve to nothing, and explicit ages in 0.0117-0.129 Ma map to no stage name (name=null); RCA_ICS_SERIES also has no 'late pleistocene'/'upper pleistocene' key. The Python comments (rca_core/standards/ics.py _SERIES_EXPLICIT_BOUNDS) acknowledge the truncation problem for series bounds but stage-level resolution still fails. Impact is contained (explicit-Ma FAD<LAD still uses the numeric value), so this is completeness, not corruption.
low_severity.evidence: "Holocene": {top_ma: 0.0, base_ma: 0.0117, era: "Cenozoic"}, ... "Chibanian": {top_ma: 0.129, base_ma: 0.774, era: "Cenozoic"},  // no Greenlandian/Northgrippian/Meghalayan; chain gap 0.0117-0.129

low_severity.title: Issue params passed but absent from strings: counts/rows/sample silently discarded
low_severity.description: Quality issues carry params that several translations never interpolate, so details vanish from the badge tooltip: quality.abundance_sum_violation passes {sample,sum} (quality.py:544 / quality.js:585) but the zh string '丰度百分比之和不等于 100%（实测：{sum}%）' omits {sample} — the zh user cannot tell WHICH level violates sum-to-100. quality.fad_lt_lad passes {count}, quality.missing_biozone {count}, quality.agreement_overflow {count} and quality.chimera_dropped {row} (quality.py:581,611,628,641), but none of the zh/en/ja strings for those keys contain the placeholders (e.g. en: 'Chimeric consensus row dropped (no single run observed this combination)'). t() only substitutes placeholders present in the string, so extra params are dropped silently.

'quality.abundance_sum_violation': '丰度百分比之和不等于 100%（实测：{sum}%）',
...
'quality.chimera_dropped':    '嵌合共识行被丢弃（无任何单次运行观察到该 FAD/LAD/生物带组合）',
low_severity.suggested_fix: Add the missing {sample}/{count}/{row} placeholders to the affected zh/en/ja strings (or stop passing unused params).

low_severity.title: Quality-badge grade text fails WCAG AA contrast in both themes

Computed ratios: light mode #10b981 on #efedeb = 2.17:1 (high), #ef4444 = 3.22:1 (low), #b45309 = 4.30:1 (mid) — all fail; dark mode #b45309 on #1f1c1a = 3.37:1 (mid) fails because the badge colors get no dark-theme override (only the pill/alert colors do, css lines 145-163). low_severity.description: Two small divergences: (1) Python wraps every dimension scorer in try/except and fails that dimension closed at 0.0 with a 'quality.scoring_failed' issue (rca_core/quality.py:998-1012); js/quality.js scoreRangeChart has no such guard - a throw propagates and is swallowed by the caller's blanket catch (js/app.js:670-675), so the entire quality badge silently disappears in direct mode while the backend still shows one.
